chunks.title: Gas leak and fire/explosion hazard
chunks.content: Never test for gas leaks with an open flame; use a commercial leak-detection soap solution. Only natural gas or propane (LP) is approved, never butane.

scenarios.condition: You smell gas near the furnace
steps: Do not light any flame or operate electrical switches
Close the external manual gas shutoff valve
Leave the building and call the gas supplier or a qualified technician

chunks.title: Carbon monoxide venting hazard
chunks.content: Improper venting or not enough combustion air can make the furnace produce dangerous carbon monoxide. The vent must be checked for blockage, leaks and spillage, and exhaust fans or dryers can affect venting.

scenarios.condition: Soot, CO alarm, or signs of improper venting
steps: Ventilate the space and leave if the CO alarm is sounding
Have a qualified technician inspect the vent and combustion air supply

chunks.title: Furnace area storage restrictions
chunks.content: Never store aerosols, cleaning products, gasoline, paint thinners, paper or rags on or near the furnace. Never run the furnace with the blower door removed.

chunks.title: Qualified personnel only
chunks.content: Only trained, qualified people should install or service the furnace. Homeowners can do basic upkeep such as cleaning or replacing air filters.

chunks.title: Freezing and anti-freeze warnings
chunks.content: The ambient temperature must stay above 32°F unless the condensate system is freeze-protected, and return air should not stay below 55°F for long. Never winterize with liquid anti-freeze because it damages the plastic parts. After a long power failure in an unheated space, have the furnace inspected before using it.

chunks.title: Safety controls must not be bypassed
chunks.content: Never bypass safety controls or adjust the pressure switches. Replace faulty controls with UPG Source 1 parts, and shut off power at the main disconnect before service instead of relying on the door interlock.

chunks.title: Combustion air contaminants
chunks.content: The furnace must use outdoor combustion air if it is near pool chemicals, laundry products, solvents, refrigerants, de-icing salts, or in hobby rooms or laundry rooms. The intake must sit away from these contaminants.

chunks.title: Massachusetts CO detector requirements
chunks.content: For sidewall vents less than 7 ft above grade in Massachusetts, hard-wired CO detectors with battery backup are required, plus a sign reading 'GAS VENT DIRECTLY BELOW' at least 8 ft above grade.

chunks.title: Clearances to combustibles and service
chunks.content: Recommended service access is 24 in. in front and 18 in. at the side. In a garage, the burners must be at least 18 in. above the floor. Keep insulation at least 12 in. from the furnace in attics.

chunks.title: Ductwork and plenum requirements
chunks.content: The minimum plenum height is 12 in. The indoor coil must be on the supply side, downstream of the furnace. Ducts that are too small raise static pressure and can overheat the heat exchanger.

chunks.title: Air filter requirements
chunks.content: Every installation needs a field-supplied filter mounted outside the furnace cabinet, never inside it. Throwaway filters are limited to 300 ft/min air velocity; faster airflow needs high-velocity filters.

chunks.title: Ratings and electrical data
chunks.content: All models are rated 95.5% AFUE and run on 115 VAC, 1-phase, 60 Hz power. Inputs range from 40 to 130 MBH, and maximum outlet air temperature is 190°F.

chunks.title: Gas pressures
chunks.content: Nominal manifold pressure is 3.5 in. w.c. for natural gas and 10.0 in. w.c. for LP. Supply overpressure must be limited to 0.5 psig.

chunks.title: Gas piping installation
chunks.content: Install a drip leg and ground union, plus an accessible manual shutoff valve within 6 ft of the furnace. Hold the valve's inlet hub with a wrench and never put a wrench on the valve body.

chunks.title: LP and high-altitude conversion
chunks.content: Converting to propane requires the factory LP kit, and above 7,999 ft the manifold pressure must be changed. Pressure switches must be swapped above 5,000 ft. Conversions must be done by an authorized dealer, and orifices must never be drilled out.

chunks.title: Electrical and thermostat wiring
chunks.content: Use a separate circuit with correct polarity and a ground, and copper conductors only. Set the thermostat heat anticipator to 0.4 A, or 6 cycles per hour on electronic thermostats. The 40 VA transformer should not power accessories.

chunks.title: Twinning and staging
chunks.content: Two identical furnaces can share one duct system: connect their TWIN terminals and common wires, and use an isolation relay. Both furnaces must be on the same power leg. Twinned airflow is about 85% of the two units combined.

chunks.title: Condensate drain system
chunks.content: The drain pan has a built-in trap, so do not add an external trap. Hoses must slope downward with no sagging loops. The drain line needs a 1/4 in. per foot slope to an open or vented drain and requires regular maintenance.

chunks.title: Vent pipe sizing and materials
chunks.content: Use Schedule 40 PVC, ABS, or approved polypropylene; metal pipe is not allowed. Minimum vent length is 5 ft, and the maximum equivalent length depends on the model, pipe size and elevation (for example, 65 ft of 2 in. pipe at sea level for 40-80K models).

chunks.title: Vent termination and clearances
chunks.content: Terminate the vent at least 12 in. above grade and the highest expected snow level, away from windows, meters and inlets. Keep the intake and exhaust in the same atmospheric zone, and never tie vents from multiple units together.

chunks.title: Combustion air supply options
chunks.content: Combustion air can come from outdoors through a pipe (direct vent), from the room around the furnace, or from a ventilated attic or crawl space. Confined spaces need openings sized per the free-area tables, and the vent itself must never end in an attic or crawl space.

chunks.title: Start-up checks and ignition sequence
chunks.content: The installer must check for gas leaks, verify input rate and verify temperature rise. On a call for heat, the inducer starts, the igniter glows for about 17 seconds, the gas valve opens, and the blower starts about 30 seconds later.

chunks.title: Temperature rise and fan delay
chunks.content: Temperature rise is measured about 6 ft from the furnace; raising blower speed lowers the rise. The blower-off delay can be set to 60, 90, 120 or 180 seconds (factory default 120) with a jumper.

chunks.title: Safety controls overview
chunks.content: The furnace has a 3 A ATO fuse, a blower door interlock, manual-reset rollout switches, two pressure switches, and an auto-reset high limit switch. It locks out after 5 limit trips in a row and retries after 1 hour.

chunks.title: Normal operation sequence
chunks.content: With the fan switch ON, the blower runs continuously at cool speed; in AUTO, the cooling fan-off delay is fixed at 60 seconds. The heating cycle retries ignition up to 3 times, then locks out for 1 hour.

chunks.title: Pre-troubleshooting checks
chunks.content: Before troubleshooting, confirm the furnace has power, the manual gas valves are open, and wiring connections are secure. Then set the thermostat above room temperature and watch how the system responds.

chunks.title: LED fault codes
chunks.content: A control board LED flashes codes to report faults. Soft lockouts reset automatically after 1 hour; hard lockouts need the power turned off and back on.

rows: Combustion air, heat exchanger; hard lockout
Gas valve ON, gas pressure, sensor, igniter

chunks.title: Fault code retrieval
chunks.content: With no thermostat call active, press LAST ERROR to show the last five codes. Hold the button more than 5 seconds to clear them; two green flashes means no codes are stored.

chunks.title: Flame sense levels
chunks.content: Normal flame sense current is about 3.7 µA DC. A low-signal warning starts at 1.5 µA, and the control locks out at 0.1 µA.

chunks.title: Intake pipe condensation
chunks.content: In hot, humid weather, condensate can form in an intake pipe that runs through conditioned space. Install the supplied intake drain hose (no sagging), and note the bird screen cannot be used with the intake drain.

tasks.title: Replace the Air Filter
tasks.description: Replace or clean the field-installed return air filter.
tasks.justification: A dirty filter restricts airflow, trips the high-limit switch (4 red flashes), and can overheat the heat exchanger.
tasks.instructions_text: Turn the thermostat off, then slide the old filter out of the external filter rack. Insert a new filter of the same size with the airflow arrow pointing toward the furnace. Never install a filter inside the furnace cabinet.

tasks.title: Maintain the Condensate Drain
tasks.description: Check the condensate hoses and drain line for clogs, sagging, and freeze risk.
tasks.justification: A blocked or sagging drain trips the pressure switch and stops the furnace from running.
tasks.instructions_text: Check that the drain hoses slope downward with no sagging loops and that water flows freely to the open drain or pump. Clear any blockage. Protect drain lines that run through freezing areas with self-regulating heat tape. Never use liquid anti-freeze.

tasks.title: Keep Vent and Intake Clear
tasks.description: Keep the outdoor vent and combustion air terminals free of snow, leaves, and obstructions.
tasks.justification: Blocked terminals trip the pressure switches and can cause unsafe venting.
tasks.instructions_text: Look at the outdoor vent and intake pipes, especially after snowfall. Clear away snow, leaves, or debris, and keep shrubs trimmed back from the terminals. Never block the intake pipe.

tasks.title: Prime Downward Vent Condensate Trap
tasks.description: Prime the condensate drain on downward-run vent pipes before heating season.
tasks.justification: An unprimed trap can let flue gas escape or stop condensate from draining.
tasks.instructions_text: Before heating season starts, pour water into the condensate traps on the downward-run intake and vent pipes until they are full.

tasks.title: Keep Furnace Area Clear
tasks.description: Keep combustibles and stored items away from the furnace.
tasks.justification: Stored chemicals and paper near the furnace create a fire hazard.
tasks.instructions_text: Move any aerosols, cleaning products, paint thinners, gasoline, rags, and paper away from the furnace. Keep attic insulation at least 12 in. away from the furnace.

tasks.title: Clean the Flame Sensor
tasks.description: Have the flame sensor cleaned when the low flame sense code appears.
tasks.justification: A dirty sensor causes failed ignition and lockouts.
tasks.instructions_text: If the LED shows continuous amber or 7-8 red flashes, a technician should clean the flame sensor, check gas flow, and confirm the flame current is above 1.5 µA.

tasks.title: Professional Furnace Inspection
tasks.description: Have a qualified technician service the furnace, including gas, combustion, venting, and safety controls.
tasks.justification: Undetected gas leaks, vent problems, or a failing heat exchanger can cause carbon monoxide or fire hazards.
tasks.instructions_text: Book a qualified service agency. The technician checks for gas leaks, manifold pressure and input rate, temperature rise, venting and CO levels, the flame, and the safety switches.

tasks.title: Inspect After Power Failure
tasks.description: Have the furnace inspected after an extended power failure if it is in an unheated space.
tasks.justification: Freezing can damage internal parts, and running a damaged unit makes it worse.
tasks.instructions_text: Do not run the furnace after a long outage in freezing conditions. Have a technician inspect the condensate system and internal parts first, and make any needed repairs.

tasks.title: Level the Furnace
tasks.description: Install the furnace level within 1/4 in. side-to-side and front-to-back.
tasks.justification: A furnace that is not level drains condensate poorly and can shut down.
tasks.instructions_text: The installer checks with a level that slope is no more than 1/4 in. in any direction and shims the furnace if needed.

re_check_triggers.description: Water pools or the furnace shuts down after being moved

tasks.title: Verify Grounding and Polarity
tasks.description: Confirm the furnace is grounded and wired with correct polarity on a dedicated circuit.
tasks.justification: Reversed polarity or a missing ground causes shock risk and 9-red-flash faults.
tasks.instructions_text: An electrician connects black to L1, white to neutral, and ground to the green screw on a separate circuit with a disconnect.

re_check_triggers.description: 9 red flashes, shock, or burning smell

tasks.title: Initial Gas Leak Check
tasks.description: Leak-test all gas connections at startup.
tasks.justification: A gas leak can cause fire or explosion.
tasks.instructions_text: The installer purges air from the gas line and checks every joint and valve with leak-detection solution while the furnace runs. Never use an open flame.

re_check_triggers.description: You smell gas near the furnace

tasks.title: Verify Input Rate and Temperature Rise
tasks.description: The installer clocks the gas meter, sets manifold pressure, and checks temperature rise.
tasks.justification: Overfiring or too little airflow causes early heat exchanger failure and CO.
tasks.instructions_text: A technician uses a manometer to measure gas pressure, clocks the meter to calculate input, and measures temperature rise 6 ft from the furnace, then adjusts blower speed to stay within the rating plate range.

re_check_triggers.description: Limit trips repeatedly or 4 red flashes appear

tasks.title: Verify Venting and Combustion Air
tasks.description: Check that the vent is properly sized, sloped and sealed, and that combustion air is adequate.
tasks.justification: Improper venting can release carbon monoxide into the home.
tasks.instructions_text: The installer confirms pipe lengths are within limits, joints are sealed, and piping slopes 1/4 in. per foot back to the furnace, then runs a spillage/CO test with exhaust fans on.

re_check_triggers.description: 3 or 6 red flashes, or a CO alarm

tasks.title: Install Condensate Drain
tasks.description: Route the condensate hoses for the furnace position and connect them to an open drain or approved pump.
tasks.justification: Wrong routing traps condensate and stops the furnace.
tasks.instructions_text: The installer reroutes the hoses to match the chosen orientation, trims excess length, caps unused openings, and runs the drain line at 1/4 in. per foot to an open drain or acid-rated condensate pump.

confidence.notes: This is an installer's manual, so there is little homeowner maintenance and no filter replacement interval is stated. No warranty section was found.
